usage: capture_cdc_benchmark.py [-h] [--port PORT]
                                [--transport {posix,usb_bulk,usb_cdc}]

                                [--suite] [--stability]
                                [--capture-seconds CAPTURE_SECONDS]
                                [--rail-avdd-uv RAIL_AVDD_UV]
                                [--rail-avss-uv RAIL_AVSS_UV]
                                [--rail-source-note RAIL_SOURCE_NOTE]
                                --expected-elf EXPECTED_ELF_SHA256
                                --expected-session EXPECTED_SESSION
                                --expected-boot-id EXPECTED_BOOT_ID

One-reader firmware benchmark: exact capture windows, immutable raw evidence.
Examples (only run after the fixture and physical port are authorized):
python3 tools/run_firmware_benchmark.py --port /dev/ttyACM0 --output-directory
OUT --label run01 --suite python3 tools/run_firmware_benchmark.py --port
/dev/ttyACM0 --output-directory OUT --label run02 --stability --mode VOLT
--rows 1 The normal suite is 32 configurations, each with 5 s warmup and 120 s
capture. --stability adds a separate 600 s capture before the optional suite.
Preparation and query/cleanup time do not count as capture. Existing external
rail evidence is required. Only explicit --rail-avdd-uv/--rail-avss-uv may
restore missing RAM calibration, in query-verified CAP with INTREF off. No CAL
SAVE, flash, reset, threshold change, input flush or modem-bit ioctl is
requested. CAPTURED means the requested window was recorded, not physical
accuracy PASS. Raw bytes are never overwritten; events record chunks, not
duplicated frames.

usage: run_cdc_matrix_failfast.py [-h] --output-directory OUTPUT_DIRECTORY
                                  --label LABEL --expected-elf EXPECTED_ELF
                                  --expected-session EXPECTED_SESSION
                                  --expected-boot-id EXPECTED_BOOT_ID
                                  --ble-address BLE_ADDRESS
                                  [--ble-adapter BLE_ADAPTER] --stop-file
                                  STOP_FILE [--usb-serial USB_SERIAL]

Run 32 independent 120-second CDC configurations, stopping on first error. The
existing collector owns the port, capture and CAP8 cleanup. This wrapper does
not read or flush USB, retry a failed case, reset, flash or save calibration.
Each case owns separate BLE/debug observers. Close and join both before the
existing real parser qualifies that case; FAIL or UNKNOWN stops the suite.
Each child has a bounded interrupt/kill fence; a killed child is never called
safe. Raw evidence is exclusive-create and retained even on failure.

usage: capture_mode_switches.py [-h] --output-directory OUTPUT_DIRECTORY
                                --label LABEL [--usb-serial USB_SERIAL]
                                [--total-seconds TOTAL_SECONDS] --expected-elf
                                EXPECTED_ELF_SHA256 --expected-session
                                EXPECTED_SESSION --expected-boot-id
                                EXPECTED_BOOT_ID

Bounded 50-transition HIL capture through the formal CDC0 owner. Uses the
current benchmark transition/CONFIG recovery implementation, never the legacy
fixture MODE helper. Exactly 50 test changes follow CAP8 preparation;
preparation and necessary CAP8 cleanup are recorded separately. A complete,
CRC-valid frame proves its wire/configuration identity, not point accuracy.
Raw records are exclusive-create; neither device input nor prior files are
flushed. No reset, USBSTREAM setter, speed command, CAL=SAVE or NVS write.

usage: capture_benchmark_ble.py [-h] --address ADDRESS [--name NAME]
                                [--adapter ADAPTER] --output-directory
                                OUTPUT_DIRECTORY --label LABEL
                                [--duration DURATION] [--stop-file STOP_FILE]

Receive-only BLE notification journal, synchronized by host monotonic clock.
No serial port or application GATT command is opened/sent. Only the three CCCD
subscriptions are requested. The existing TX/BTX configuration is left intact.
Run before the serial benchmark; wait for <label>.ble.ready.json, then launch
the serial suite. Finish with --stop-file (create that file), SIGINT or
SIGTERM. The duration is a finite total session ceiling, including
connection/cleanup. No reconnect is attempted. Offline analysis must
distinguish unconnected time from connected zero-frame windows and callback
time from over-air reception.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --address ADDRESS
  --name NAME
  --adapter ADAPTER
  --output-directory OUTPUT_DIRECTORY
  --label LABEL
  --duration DURATION
  --stop-file STOP_FILE

usage: observe_cdc_debug.py [-h] --output-directory OUTPUT_DIRECTORY --label
                            LABEL --usb-serial USB_SERIAL [--usb-pid USB_PID]
                            [--duration DURATION]
                            [--enumerate-seconds ENUMERATE_SECONDS]
                            [--stop-file STOP_FILE]

Independent Linux CDC debug observer; never a formal DATA/CTRL collector.
Select explicit 303a:4041 or 303a:4042, stable serial and CDC interface 2
using read-only sysfs metadata. No commands, USBBOOT, input flush or modem-bit
ioctl. Opening a CDC tty can cause OS line-state requests; firmware requires
CDC DTR for debug delivery. This is not a promise that OS open behaviour is
side-effect free, nor evidence that the scientific bulk stream has arrived on
the PC.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --output-directory OUTPUT_DIRECTORY
  --label LABEL
  --usb-serial USB_SERIAL
  --usb-pid USB_PID     4041 vendor bulk; use 0x4042 for dual CDC
  --duration DURATION
  --enumerate-seconds ENUMERATE_SECONDS
  --stop-file STOP_FILE
